DeployBot: Scheduled deploy v2.14.1 -> prod at 2025-07-12 23:00 UTC. Change window 23:00-23:30 UTC. Canary in eu-west-1 first. Auto-pin option available; rollback policy: immediate on canary fail.
Naomi (Eng Releases): Heads-up for comms & support teams — this one touches runtime kernel patch and a serving config tweak. Expected low risk but potential transient latencies during warmup.
Alice Chen: Can we pin Dedicated/Enterprise customers to v2.14.0 during the rollout window? A couple customers asked for strict version stability.
Marcus Nguyen: We can do per-customer pinning. Proposal: pin enterprise customers for 3 hours post-deploy, then auto-unpin if no issues.
Ben Rodriguez: Safety thresholds I want on DeployBot: canary latency >18% vs baseline OR error rate >1% absolute -> hold and notify. Also CPU/GPU >82% for 2 consecutive minutes should pause.
SupportOps: Draft statuspage snippet below — please review for tone and localization.
SupportOps: ```Scheduled maintenance: We will deploy a minor runtime update (v2.14.1) to production starting 23:00 UTC. We expect up to 15 minutes of increased latency for a subset of requests during canary and warmup. Impact: degraded response times (no data loss). Regions affected: eu-west-1 initially, then global. ETA: 23:30 UTC. If you rely on pinned model versions, please expect no forced model changes.```
Naomi (Eng Releases): +1 on that wording. Add a line for APAC hours localization and include contact link.
Alice Chen: Suggest adding a short customer email snippet for Support to send to enterprise tenants who asked for notice.
SupportOps: Email snippet (paste-ready):
SupportOps: "Subject: Scheduled maintenance — runtime update (v2.14.1) on 12 Jul 2025
Hello <CustomerName>,
We will be performing a scheduled maintenance deploy to our inference runtime on 12 Jul 2025 at 23:00 UTC. During the rollout we may observe brief increases in latency for a subset of requests while canaries and nodes warm up. No inference requests will be dropped and model pins will be respected for enterprise plans. If you have strict latency SLAs, reply to this message and we will coordinate a dedicated change window.
Regards,
Redwood Support"
Marcus Nguyen: For the deployment playbook: start canary (5% traffic), wait 10m, check tracing for 503s/errors, ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 5m checks. If any hold condition, do automatic rollback to v2.14.0 and trigger incident channel.
Ben Rodriguez: Add tracing smoke checks: sample a 200-request set of hot prompts and verify median latency < baseline *1.18 and p95 < baseline *1.25. If exceeded, hold.
Naomi (Eng Releases): Good. Who will own the customer notifications? Alice?
Alice Chen: I can own enterprise notifications. SupportOps — please prepare the statuspage update and localized versions for APAC/EU (ja/zh/fr). I will send the enterprise email list.
SupportOps: Will do. I'll post the localized snippets in #support-drafts and tag you.
Marcus Nguyen: Also recommend we enable automatic pin for any customers that have "lock_on_release" flag set — quick safety net.
Naomi (Eng Releases): Agree — enable auto-pin for lock_on_release accounts for the first 3 hours by default. We can relax later.
Ben Rodriguez: One more: add a DeployBot webhook to create a follow-up thread if rollback happens so oncall + eng-releases get immediate context.
DeployBot: Canary start initiated at 1758800065 — 5% traffic routed to eu-west-1. Monitoring hooks active. :eyes:
